author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page lists veterinarians by specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory answers the inverse of the vet list: every specialty by its stored name, and under each the veterinarians holding it, on one page.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it
A veterinarian holding a specialty is shown by full name with given name before family name (for example "Helen Leary")
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page is organised by specialty, not a second copy of the full veterinarian roster
All specialties render together on one page with no pagination
non_goals: Creating, renaming, or reassigning specialties or veterinarians (NG-2 unchanged)
notes: Read-only inverse view of REQ-VET-001. Product decision to include the read-only specialty view was made by the user as product owner; NG-2 explicitly unchanged. REQ-VET-002 is withdrawn and its ID is not reused.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only inverse projection of the vet↔specialty relation already modelled in the vet package. It reuses the established server-rendered pattern in full (system-design.md Overview + Contracts VetController row): a @Controller GET method reads a repository, assembles a Model, and renders a Thymeleaf template under templates/vets/. No new module, persistence pattern, or cross-feature model — the Specialty and Vet entities and VetRepository already co-live in the vet package, and Vet.getSpecialties() already exposes the association sorted by name.
integration_points: New GET /specialties.html route added to the existing VetController (same package, same repository dependency); no new controller class needed
Model exposes specialties each paired with its holding veterinarians; the template mirrors vetList.html's full-name expression ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} for AC2
Grouping/inversion is application logic in the controller: iterate VetRepository.findAll(), collect the distinct specialties and, per specialty, the vets whose getSpecialties() contains it

patterns.description: existing showVetList: @Controller GET reads VetRepository, builds Model, returns a templates/vets/ view name — the pattern the new route follows unchanged (minus pagination)
full-name rendering and the specialty-name loop the new template mirrors, inverted

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 build test walks templates and compares message-bundle keys across all locales; any new #{key} in specialtyList.html that is absent from even one of the ~11 locale bundles fails the build (checkFormat/check stage), not a test assertion
risks.mitigation: add every new message key to every messages/messages_*.properties bundle in the same slice; prefer reusing existing keys (#{specialties}, #{name}, #{none}) where they fit

risks.risk: a veterinarian holding multiple specialties correctly appears under each — but a naive grouping could also emit a phantom bucket for vets with no specialty, contradicting AC3 (the page lists specialties, not a no-specialty catch-all)
risks.mitigation: drive the grouping from the specialties present on the vets, not from the vet roster; a vet with zero specialties contributes to no group and does not appear

notes: Deferred design question resolved: the inverse view lives in the existing vet package and templates/vets/ (specialtyList.html alongside vetList.html) — it earns no new package. Rationale: Specialty and Vet are one aggregate area already co-located in the vet package; a projection of their relation splitting into a new package would add a module boundary and a second data-access path for a pure read view, against the package's single-repository shape (system-design.md Package Structure). Second decision: the specialty set is derived from VetRepository.findAll() and inverted in the controller — NO new SpecialtyRepository. NG-2 forbids creating/renaming specialties from the UI, so no reachable application state produces a specialty held by zero vets; deriving from the vets is therefore behaviourally complete for AC1 'every specialty the clinic knows', and a SpecialtyRepository would be speculative generality for an unreachable state. If a future slice adds a specialty write path, that reintroduces the question — flag it then. No system-design.md edit or ADR: this is a routine application of existing patterns, not a change to the durable cross-feature model. IDE oracle N/A on this run (not in tool set); the covered claim is grounded in direct Read of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Specialty, and vetList.html.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory
summary: The specialty directory presents every specialty by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it, on one page. A veterinarian holding no specialty is absent from the directory, because the page is organised by specialty rather than a second copy of the vet roster.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then each specialty is listed by its stored name with the veterinarians holding it
given a veterinarian holding a specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian is shown by full name, given name before family name
given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under none of the specialties and so is absent from the directory
given every specialty the clinic knows, when the directory is opened, then all of them are shown on one page with no pagination
non_goals: creating, renaming, or reassigning specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: Supersedes the prior REQ-SPEC-001 prd-entry: the earlier prose ("gathered under no specialty rather than omitted") and acceptance criterion inverted the product owner's intent. A veterinarian with zero specialties is absent from the page, not shown in a visible no-specialty bucket. The shipped implementation already has the correct behavior; this record and the docs/prd.md wording fix align the PRD with it. Wording-only change; no other PRD edits.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: All user-visible dynamic content in specialtyList.html renders via auto-escaping th:text (entry.key.name and the ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} full-name expression); no th:utext or unescaped sink, so stored specialty/vet names cannot yield stored XSS
SpecialtyRepository.findAll() and VetRepository.findAll() are parameterless Spring Data derived queries; no user input reaches any query, no SQL/template injection surface

New /specialties.html endpoint takes no request parameters and exposes only non-sensitive public directory data, consistent with the existing public /vets.html; no new authz boundary or PII/secret exposure
No new dependencies introduced, so no supply-chain change to vet
Unbounded findAll() (no pagination) is a product decision over a small fixed dataset; a resource-exhaustion/DOS concern out of scope for this review with no confident exploit path

Affected names: specialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians, specialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName, specialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansWithoutSpecialtyUnderNoSpecialty, specialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePageWithoutPagination.

Test name specialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansWithoutSpecialtyUnderNoSpecialty says 'group under no specialty', implying a visible no-specialty bucket, but the assertion verifies absence (not(containsString("James Carter"))). author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: specialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName asserts only containsString("Helen Leary"), which is already covered by specialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians. No unique behavior is documented and the test adds maintenance cost without increasing coverage.
findings.fix: Remove the test, or replace it with an assertion that specifically validates first-name-before-last-name ordering — for example, asserting the rendered text matches a pattern where the given name precedes the family name — so the test documents behavior distinct from the first test.

findings.description: Each vet span is rendered as vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName + ' ', appending a trailing space after every name. When multiple vets appear under one specialty the result is run-on text with no visual separator between names (for example 'Alice Smith Bob Jones '). Browsers collapse whitespace so it is not a visible defect in simple cases, but the intent — multiple names separated clearly — is not expressed.
findings.fix: Separate multiple names with a comma and space, or render each name on its own line, so the separator is explicit rather than implied by whitespace collapse.

findings.description: findAll() carries no @Cacheable annotation. The equivalent VetRepository.findAll() uses @Cacheable("vets"). Specialties are static reference data; without caching every request to /specialties.html issues a database query, while the vet fetch in the same handler is served from cache.
findings.fix: Add @Cacheable("specialties") to findAll(), consistent with the caching pattern on VetRepository.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyRepository follows the Repository<Specialty, Integer> pattern used by VetRepository — same interface, same @Transactional(readOnly = true), same return type
Constructor injection in VetController is correct; no @Autowired needed with a single constructor
Javadoc on holdersOf explains the name-based matching decision, making the design legible to the next reader
LinkedHashMap correctly preserves insertion order after the sorted stream, so specialties reach the template in alphabetical order
Test names follow the BDD sentence convention established in the existing suite
checkFormat passed; no formatting violations

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Read-only inverse projection of the vet↔specialty relation in the vet package, following the established server-rendered pattern (system-design.md Overview + Contracts). Correction to the superseded line-4 decision: the specialty set is read from storage via a dedicated read-only SpecialtyRepository (Repository<Specialty,Integer>, @Transactional(readOnly=true) findAll()), NOT derived from VetRepository.findAll(). The schema permits a specialty row with zero holders, and the acceptance criterion lists every specialty by its stored name; deriving from the vet roster would silently omit a zero-holder specialty. SpecialtyRepository is a plain application of the existing Spring Data read-repository pattern already used by VetRepository and PetTypeRepository — no new module, persistence pattern, or cross-feature model.
integration_points: docs/system-design.md Contracts: added a SpecialtyRepository row (Implements REQ-SPEC-001) whose Purpose carries the guarantee that a zero-holder specialty still appears; corrected the VetController row to Implements REQ-VET-001, REQ-SPEC-001 with a Purpose covering the /specialties.html directory route
docs/system-design.md Package Structure: vet/ tree line now reads 'repositories' (two: VetRepository, SpecialtyRepository)

patterns.description: the Spring Data read-repository pattern SpecialtyRepository follows verbatim — same Repository<T,Integer> interface, same @Transactional(readOnly=true), same findAll() shape

notes: Supersedes line 4. That record's second decision ('NO new SpecialtyRepository; deriving from the vets is behaviourally complete') was wrong and was overridden by the orchestrator: it assumed NG-2 makes a zero-holder specialty unreachable, but the relational schema independently permits a specialty row with no holders, and AC1 requires every specialty by its STORED name — so deriving from the vet roster omits it. The derive-from-vets alternative is therefore considered-and-rejected on requirements grounds, not an open architectural trade-off; once the AC pins 'stored name' plus the zero-holder case (product-requirements-expert is adding that AC to docs/prd.md in parallel), the storage-read is required by spec. No ADR: the choice is requirement-forced and is a routine reuse of the existing read-repository pattern, not a hard-to-reverse or surprising trade-off, so a why-ADR would add no design information the Contracts row does not already carry. The zero-holder Javadoc spec-claim the doc-reviewer flagged (src/, not my scope) resolves once the parallel PRD zero-holder AC lands, which anchors SpecialtyRepository's REQ-SPEC-001. No design-doc-autofix records to audit this dispatch. IDE oracle N/A on this run (not in tool set); grounded in direct Read of SpecialtyRepository, VetRepository, and the shipped contracts table.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The prd-entry at handoff line 21 declares test_names: ["theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowSpecialtyWithNoHoldersAsHeldByNone"] as the normative contract for the zero-holder AC5. That method does not exist. Two existing tests partially exercise the criterion in passing — theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians asserts containsString("surgery") (stored name present) and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinarianWithNoSpecialtyFromDirectory asserts containsString("none") — but both tests are named for different acceptance criteria (AC1 and AC4 respectively). No test is named as a specification for AC5: given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the directory is opened, then it is listed by stored name and shown as held by none. A future reader cannot identify which test pins AC5, and a regression in the zero-holder path would break tests whose names point elsewhere.

The specialtyList.html template's iterStat.last branch now emits ', ' between names when a specialty has two or more holders. The current fixture provides at most one holder per specialty (Helen Leary under radiology; surgery has none), so the comma-separator path — the false branch of iterStat.last ? '' : ', ' — is never executed by any test. The production behavior for a multi-holder specialty is unexercised. A second holder added to either radiology or surgery in the fixture, paired with a containsString assertion for the name-comma-name pattern, would pin the branch.
